The "Yaqdah" system is a technology-driven initiative designed to tackle road accidents caused by driver drowsiness, a critical safety issue in Libya and worldwide. Utilizing AI and smartphone-based computer vision, it provides a low-cost, efficient alternative to expensive specialized hardware

The system continuously monitors the driver's facial expressions and eye movements to detect signs of drowsiness, sleep, or inattention. Going beyond standard audio alerts, it features an integrated generative AI model that acts as an intelligent co-pilot. This AI verbally interacts with the driver through dynamic messages to re-engage them cognitively

Additionally, Yaqdah offers a comprehensive safety suite. This includes suggesting nearby rest areas upon detecting fatigue and an emergency alert system that automatically sends a distress signal if an imminent danger is sensed and the driver is unresponsive

Built with modern tools like Flutter for cross-platform performance and Google ML Kit for computer vision, the system employs Gemini AI for interactive dialogue and local data storage (SQLite) to ensure privacy and offline functionality. The project demonstrates a practical application of modern technology to enhance road safety and save lives
